parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or gender expression, no documented border/document friction, no universal facility or ward rule, an official posture of cooperation (UPR acceptances, tourism ministry welcome campaign), and a visible scene with Pride since 2003 are meaningful positives. Against that: documented state-tolerated police targeting of trans women in one city (extortion, forced humiliating bathing) plus a pattern of street harassment (135+ cases) and a survey where ~38% of trans women reported arrest, mostly for being trans — tier-2 targeting, though geographically and occupationally narrow and not shown as a general campaign against visitors. Custody placement is an open question (surgery-gated transfer, no published rule), which is light, not exposure. No non-discrimination statute and unremedied paper protections leave recourse thin. Violence records are monitoring counts, not rates; no killings or organised pogrom documented. Net: elevated but not high risk.
